registers.method_note: Registers are scanned images; figures were read by OCR and parsed line by line. For every month with a legible printed total, the parsed BOCC line items summed to 94.7%-100.1% of the printed total (most months 99.6%-100%). Only the Board of County Commissioners section is counted (the CVB and CDC sections are excluded). Vendor names were merged across spelling variants (older registers truncate names at 25 characters). top_vendors excludes payees that are other governments, constitutional officers, tax/payroll/benefit remittances, pass-through transfers, banks/debt service, title/escrow agents and law-firm trust payments; top_payees_all shows the unfiltered ranking. Amounts are net of voided checks listed in the register.

thresholds.rule: Orders up to $3,500: no quotes; $3,500-$10,000: three telephone quotes; $10,000-$150,000: three written quotes; over $150,000: competitive solicitation procedures required. Board approval required for purchases and agreements over $150,000 (County Manager authority up to $150,000). Emergency contracts over $150,000 may be authorized by the County Manager with the Chairman and ratified by the Board at its next regular meeting. Change orders exceeding a cumulative 10% of the original contract or $150,000 require approval by the signatory for that contract value. Single/sole-source intent must be posted on the county website for at least 15 business days. Piggyback and cooperative contracts (e.g., state term, Sourcewell) are allowed.
thresholds.notes: Procurement Manual cover dated October 2026 (current version on the county Purchasing page); thresholds in earlier versions covering FY2023-FY2026 were not checked.

thresholds.rule: Orders up to $3,499.99: written estimate/quote; $3,500-$100,000: three comparative quotes; over $100,000: competitive solicitation procedures required. City Commission approval over $100,000 (City Manager up to $100,000). Emergency purchases under $200,000 by City Manager authorization; over $200,000 require a Commission agenda item before payment. Change orders (additive or deductive) exceeding the lesser of 10% of contract price or $100,000 cumulative require Commission approval.
thresholds.notes: Purchasing Policy and Procedures Manual as revised and adopted 2025-10-28 (Resolution 20251028.3); it superseded a version last revised 2025-03-01, which was not reviewed.

thresholds.rule: General (non-utility) purchases: up to $5,000 no quotes; $5,000-$24,999.99 three written quotes plus PO; $25,000 and above competitive solicitation and City Council approval. Utility purchases: up to $10,000 no quotes; $10,000-$25,000 written quotes, sole-source or emergency justification; $25,000-$99,999.99 goods require Council approval with three written quotes; $100,000 and above competitive solicitation.
thresholds.notes: City "Do Business with the City" page; the full Procurement Manual is linked there (https://www.pcbfl.gov/DocumentCenter/View/1778) but was not downloaded. A 2024-07-25 agenda memo states the City Manager's change-order authority is $25,000 per change order.

thresholds.rule: Purchases of commodities or services over $35,000 per year require City Commission approval, and commodity purchases of $35,000 or more require formal advertised bids to the lowest responsive, responsible bidder; $3,500-$35,000 City Manager approval; $3,500 or less Finance Director. Exemptions include utility operation/maintenance purchases up to $100,000 and emergencies (purchases of $35,000+ authorized by City Manager, subject to an extraordinary vote at the next meeting). Sole-source purchases limited to $34,999 per year. Additional requirements for public works projects of $250,000 or more.
thresholds.notes: Procurement Policy approved 2025-12-09; earlier policy not reviewed.

thresholds.rule: Up to $3,500: department head; $3,500-$25,000: three verbal quotes; $25,000-$150,000: three written quotes, no Council vote required; over $150,000: competitive bids and a Council vote (exceptions for emergencies and certain utilities/grant-funded projects). Emergency expenditures over $250,000 have additional approval steps.

Expenditures over $8,000 require competitive bids (normally advertised); $3,000-$8,000 require three verbal quotes. Council may waive competitive bidding by majority vote for single-source, federal/state agency or one-time auction purchases.
thresholds.notes: Ordinance 612, adopted 2013-12-10, posted on the city site in 2025; no later amendment was found, but one may exist.

notes: Contract amounts are the amounts in the agenda recommendation or agenda title (or the attached item memo/resolution where noted). An agenda item is a proposal; the records were not each checked against minutes. Known cases where a proposal changed are recorded in notes (e.g., PCB pickleball bids rejected 2026-04-09; Panama City PC24-050 re-awarded; Panama City PC25-001 amount changed between agendas).

Bay County awards were taken from every BOCC regular-meeting agenda from 2022-10-04 through 2026-10-20 (97 meetings) on the county PrimeGov portal. Items of $250,000 or more were captured, plus all change orders and emergency purchases of note. Grant agreements, budget amendments, land transactions, SHIP loans and bonds were excluded.

Panama City (126 commission agendas, 2022-10 to 2026-10) and Panama City Beach (94 council agendas, 2022-10 to 2026-10) were reviewed in full for items of about $250,000 or more. For Lynn Haven, Callaway, Mexico Beach and Parker, smaller awards (about $100,000 and up) are included because few contracts reach $250,000.

Method labels are based on the wording of the agenda item: "ITB"/"base bid"/"low bidder" = competitive sealed bid; "RFQ"/"top ranked" = qualifications-based selection; "task order" = work under an existing continuing-services contract; "piggyback"/Sourcewell/FSA/OMNIA/City of Tallahassee contract = cooperative or piggyback purchase. For Bay County items identified only by contract number, the type comes from the county's bid posting at baycountyfl.gov/bids.aspx where available (link in notes). Where the source does not say, the method is "Not stated".

Vendors that appear most often across governments in this period: Marshall Brothers Construction & Engineering, Roberts and Roberts, C.W. Roberts Contracting, Anderson Columbia, Mainline Construction, Gulf Coast Utility Contractors, Royal American Construction, Dewberry Engineers, Mott MacDonald, Panhandle Engineering, CDR Maguire and Hagerty Consulting (disaster-recovery consulting).

Bay County check-register top vendors are cash paid in the months covered, not contract value; large construction payments in a year reflect work performed on contracts awarded earlier (e.g., Weeks Marine's $25.3M in FY2025 on the $27.2M Mexico Beach beach restoration contract 24-45).

Discrepancy: Bay County bid posting 24-22 (artificial reef) lists Walter Marine, Inc. as bid recipient, while the 2024-10-01 BOCC agenda recommends awarding Contract 24-22 to Weeks Marine for $492,750.
gaps: No check register or vendor-payment list was found for any city (Panama City, Panama City Beach, Callaway, Springfield, Parker, Mexico Beach). Lynn Haven agenda packets include a filtered "Check Reconciliation" (warrant list) of larger checks; see registers if present.

Bay County check registers were only found attached to BOCC agendas from January 2024 onward. FY2023 is not covered. FY2024 covers 7 of 12 months (Jan and Apr-Sep 2024; Oct-Dec 2023 and Feb-Mar 2024 are missing). FY2025 is missing February 2025. FY2026 runs through July 2026 (Aug-Sep 2026 had not been presented as of 2026-10-20). Missing months could be requested from the Clerk of Court.

The Bay County registers list the BOCC's disbursements only. Spending by the Sheriff, Clerk, Property Appraiser, Tax Collector and Supervisor of Elections shows up as lump-sum transfers to those offices; their own vendor payments are not included.
Bay County FY2023 agendas (Oct 2022 to Feb 2024) were read from the first 25 pages of each compiled agenda packet; a few items whose text fell outside those pages may be missing.
Springfield: meeting pages on springfieldfl.net do not include agenda documents, and the document library needs a staff login. No Springfield contracts or purchasing thresholds were captured.

Callaway: most agenda packets are scanned images and agenda titles carry no dollar amounts, so only three awards were captured from the few text-searchable packets. No Callaway purchasing threshold was found.
Mexico Beach and Parker: council minutes are scanned images and were read by OCR. Coverage depends on OCR quality and on which minutes are posted.

Panama City Beach: many council agenda titles have no dollar amount. Amounts were pulled from linked item memos and resolutions for the larger items, but some regular-agenda contracts (e.g., Front Beach Road Segment 3 change order 11, the CRA program management agreement with DRMP, the CentralSquare ERP agreement, the 2026 command bus vendor) have no amount here.

Original contract amounts for several change orders (e.g., Bay County juvenile courthouse addition, PCB Front Beach Road Segment 3, Panama City Martin Theatre and SRF Area F1) were not in the FY2023-FY2026 agendas reviewed, so percentage increases could not be computed for them.
Procurement portals (Bay County OpenGov, DemandStar, BidNet, Bonfire) were not used as data sources. Awards were taken from agendas, plus the county's own bids.aspx postings for solicitation type.
